newsitem.title: USA: Kodak to split Asia Pacific region.
newsitem.headline: Kodak to split Asia Pacific region.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said on Monday it would divide its existing Asia Pacific region into the two new regions of Japan and Asia Pacific, in order to take full advantage of opportunities in the area.
The company also said Robert Smith, vice president and general manager of its Asia Pacific region, would retire effective April 1, 1997.
Smith would head the new Japan region until his retirement, Kodak said, adding it would conduct an internal and external search for his replacement.

Edward Hoppe, vice president and general manager, marketing companies, for Kodak's European, African and Middle Eastern Region, was named vice president and general manager of the new Asia Pacific region, it said.
Kodak said the new regional structure would improve company focus and management attention on the growth opportunities in the Asia and the Pacific rim area.
Japan needed to be a separate region because it was the second largest photography market in the world, Kodak said.

The Asia Pacific region, to be headquartered in Singapore, would consist off all countries in that part of the world other than Japan and greater China, Kodak said. Greater China was another separate region.
Hoppe would be replaced by David Wilson, general manager of Kodak's Nordic cluster, Kodak said.
